detail: Read help page (TLC lead-chelation trial). Wide form: one row per child (id, trt) with lead levels at weeks 0/1/4/6 as columns y0,y1,y4,y6; the grouping unit (child) is no column of the loaded table (#23 wide rule).
Read help page. Wide form of the TLC data (id, trt, y1-y4 occasion columns) with weeks 1/4/6 set to missing (MAR) for illustration; one row per child, grouping unit no column (#23 wide rule).

Read help page (bronchopulmonary dysplasia, 223 low-birth-weight infants). One row per infant (bpd, weight, gestage, toxemia); a cross-sectional logistic design with no repeated-measures or cluster column.

Read help page (Thall & Vail progabide seizure trial). Wide form: one row per patient (id, trt, age) with baseline y0 and four post-randomization counts y1-y4 as columns; grouping unit (patient) no column (#23 wide rule). The long version is stata_epilepsy.
Read help page. One row per patient (id, trt, age, y) holding only the final 2-week seizure count; no repeated measures, no grouping column.

Read help page (exercise-therapy strength study; Freund, Littell & Spector 1986). Wide form: one row per patient (id, group) with strength at days 0-12 as columns y0..y12; grouping unit no column (#23 wide rule). The long version is stata_exercise.

Read help page (Potthoff & Roy 1964 orthodontic growth). Wide form: one row per child (id, gender) with the distance at ages 8/10/12/14 as columns y1-y4; grouping unit no column (#23 wide rule). The long version is nlme Orthodont.

Read help page (coronary-heart-disease risk factors; Selvin 1995). 16 rows, an aggregate cross-classification of smoke x bp x behavior with CHD case counts and person-years; each row a unique covariate cell, a fixed-effects Poisson rate model with no clustering unit.

Read help page (Snedecor & Cochran leprosy antibiotic trial). Wide form: one row per patient (drug, pre-count y1, post-count y2); the within-patient occasion is spread across two columns, so the grouping unit is no column (#23 wide rule).

Read help page (NCGS serum cholesterol; Wei & Lachin 1984). Wide form: one row per patient (group, id) with cholesterol at baseline and months 6/12/20/24 as columns y1-y5; grouping unit no column (#23 wide rule).
Read help page (Box 1950 rat weight-gain growth curves). Wide form: one row per rat (id, group) with weight at weeks 0-4 as columns y1-y5; grouping unit no column (#23 wide rule).

Read help page (respiratory-illness trial; Stokes, Davis & Koch 1995). Wide form: one row per patient (clinic, id, trt) with respiratory status at baseline and visits 1-4 as columns y0-y4; grouping unit no column (#23 wide rule). The long version is in geepack/registry respiratory.
Read help page (bladder-cancer tumor recurrence; Wei, Lin & Weissfeld 1989). One row per patient (id, trt, tumor) at the month-18 visit only; no repeated measures, no grouping column.

Read help page (auranofin rheumatoid-arthritis trial; Bombardier et al. 1986). Wide form: one row per patient (id, trt, age) with the ordinal arthritis scale at months 0/2/4/6 as columns y1-y4; grouping unit no column (#23 wide rule).

Read help page (Alachua County mental-impairment study; Agresti 2010 Table 3.3). One row per adult (id, le, ses, y); a cross-sectional 4-level ordinal regression with no repeated measures or cluster column.

Read help page (Connecticut Child Surveys; Zahner et al. 1993). One row per child (cid, health, single) with the parent and teacher externalizing reports as two columns (pextern, textern); the informant cluster is spread across columns, so no grouping column in the loaded table (#23 wide rule).

Read help page: the same DMPA amenorrhea trial as amenorrhea.dta, restructured for transition/dropout models with a lagged-response column (prevy, amenorrhea status at the previous occasion) and an observed/missing indicator (r). Same women and response as amenorrhea.dta (the primary long form), so a derived twin of a same-source object.

No documentation page; the delimited file has no header (pandas named the columns from the first data row) and is a 51-row aggregate count table (gender, age-cohort indicator dummies with '.' missing, and occasion count columns) of the Muscatine obesity data (Woolson & Clarke 1984 Table 10). The individual-level long form is muscatine.dta (registry), so this is a same-source aggregate. RULE GAP: an aggregate contingency table with no header and no companion documentation; filed as derived of muscatine.dta rather than attempting a model on unnamed columns.
